verdict: Lend selectively in Solapur sugar and ethanol — integrated mills with distillery or CBG capacity and clean cane-payment records are OK; stand-alone mills bidding the highest cane price are Avoid.
title: Solapur Sugar & Ethanol: a note to the credit manager
narrative: **Cash arrives in a lumpy seasonal cycle while cane payment is a social and political obligation that must be met fast.** Onkar Sugar is publicly promising the highest cane price in Solapur and payment within eight days [1] — so when a proposal lands, check the mill's own declared cane price against the district's prevailing rate; if a borrower is matching the highest price in the district, ask how it funds the gap between crush and sugar sale.

## Where value and cash sit
Value sits in recovery rate, distillery share of revenue and the speed of cane settlement. **The single most revealing number in this industry is cane arrears.** Solapur farmers are already squeezed by pending cane bills from the last season [3] — so pull the Sugar Commissioner's arrears list for the borrower before sanction; if the mill appears with arrears, ask for the settlement schedule and hold disbursal against it. Peer evidence says integrated mills with ethanol absorb the cycle better: ICRA notes remunerative ethanol prices and interest subvention for debt-funded distillery capex help prevent cane arrears piling up [10].

## What has changed now
Two local facts pull in opposite directions. **Solapur's CBG capacity is set to rise to 363 tonnes per day [2] — that is the growth story, and it is real capex demand.** Against it, Maharashtra electricity demand grew 6.0% Apr-to-date versus India's 9.5% [D], a local stress signal, and bank credit nationally is running -7.0% YoY against output +5.1% [D]. Peer results are healthy — Triveni reports improved profitability and reduced debt on strong sugar and distillery margins [5], and EID Parry's average realization rose to INR 51.2 per kilogram from INR 43.7 per kilogram [6] — but these are peers, not Solapur mills, and the rating reports on cane cyclicality are undated [8][10].

## Who to pursue, and how to grow safely
**Pursue integrated mills adding distillery or CBG capacity, and CBG project SPVs tied to an existing mill's cane supply [2].** Structure term debt against the distillery or CBG unit with a DSRA and a cane-availability covenant; take monthly cane-crushing and recovery data, monthly ethanol dispatch volumes, and the Sugar Commissioner's arrears position every month. Avoid stand-alone mills with no ethanol offtake and no arrears-free record.

## Early-warning signs
- Cane arrears appearing on the Commissioner's list (monthly) -> freeze fresh disbursal and ask for a settlement plan. - Declared cane price above the district's prevailing rate (season start) -> re-underwrite the funding gap. - Recovery rate falling below the borrower's own three-year average (monthly) -> cut drawing power. - Ethanol or CBG offtake delays (monthly) -> ask for the offtake contract status.
